# Catudvārajātaka (Ja 439)

**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
In this Pali version, the Bodhisatta is not Mittavinda but appears separately as a deity (*devaputta* / *devarājā*) who observes his suffering [JIABS 2013; Fausböll 1887].
The tale represents an earlier iteration of the narrative cycle shared with the *Losaka Jātaka* (Ja 41) and the Northern Buddhist legend of Maitrakanyaka attested in the *Avadānaśataka* (no. 36), the *Divyāvadāna*, and Kṣemendra's *Avadānakalpalatā* [JIABS 2013; Kudo 2004; Grünwedel 1900]. While later Sanskrit avadānas transform Maitrakanyaka into the Bodhisattva whose suffering sparks universal compassion leading to rebirth in Tuṣita heaven, the Pali Jātaka maintains Mittavinda's separate, unredeemed status [JIABS 2013; Grünwedel 1900]. Elements of the *Catudvāra* and *Losaka* Jātakas are also blended in Kang Senghui's Chinese translation in the *Liudu ji jing* [Huynh 2016]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 10 matches exclusively within the Pali tradition, sharing over 1,500 characters with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Catuttho bhāgo), with no cross-language matches above the alignment threshold [DharmaNexus].
